title: Praying for the One We Have

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And Abraham said to God, "If only Ishmael might live under your blessing!" - Gen 17:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a tender, honest moment. God has just promised a son through Sarah, but Abraham's heart goes to the son he already has: "If only Ishmael might live under your blessing!" For thirteen years Ishmael had been Abraham's only child, the boy he loved. And here Abraham pleads for him - not doubting God's new promise so much as loving the son already in his arms.

There is something deeply human and good here. Abraham brings his real concern to God. He doesn't hide his love for Ishmael or pretend he only cares about the promised child. He prays honestly for the one who is already before him.

This is a model of honest, particular prayer. We can bring our specific loves and worries to God - this child, this person, this concern that fills our hearts. God is not annoyed by our particular affections; He invites us to name them before Him.

And how does God respond? As we'll see, He doesn't rebuke Abraham's love for Ishmael - He honours it, promising to bless Ishmael too, while holding firm to His plan for Isaac. God can hold our heartfelt prayers and His larger purposes together. "Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you" (1 Pet 5:7). Whoever is on your heart today, bring them honestly to God. He hears, and He cares about the ones you love.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Who is on your heart that you need to bring honestly to God?
- Do you trust God with both your specific loves and His larger plans?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, I bring You the ones I love by name, with all my honest concern for them. Thank You that You hear my particular prayers and care about those on my heart. I trust them to You.
Amen.
